result.rationale: In refreshOAuthTokens, the credential-sync path returns the raw fetch Response ('const response = await fetch(...); return response;'). The Hubspot CalendarService assigns this directly as HubspotToken ('const hubspotRefreshToken: HubspotToken = await refreshOAuthTokens(...)') without any parsing, then reads hubspotRefreshToken.refresh_token/refresh_token fields — which are undefined on a Response object. So with sync enabled, the refresh path stores a credential with undefined token fields. This is verifiable from the diff itself.

judged_text: With credential sync enabled, refreshOAuthTokens returns a raw fetch Response but the result is assigned directly to hubspotRefreshToken and consumed as a HubspotToken object, so refreshToken/accessToken are undefined on this path. The service computes expiry from an undefined timestamp and persists a credential whose token fields are undefined, reporting a successful refresh while storing a broken credential that fails all subsequent Hubspot API calls.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts`, when credential sync is enabled it does `return response;` where `response` is the raw `fetch(...)` Response object. In `packages/app-store/hubspot/lib/CalendarService.ts`, `hubspotRefreshToken: HubspotToken = await refreshOAuthTokens(...)` assumes the returned value is a `HubspotToken` (the old behavior of `hubspotClient.oauth.tokensApi.createToken(...)`). On the sync-enabled path, `hubspotRefreshToken` will instead be a `Response`, so token fields (e.g., access/refresh/expiry-related fields) will be undefined and any subsequent expiry computation / credential persistence will be wrong. The diff shows no JSON parsing of the Response in the hubspot code path, making this a verifiable correctness defect.
